generator.program.note: The order's woody program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: Fabaceae's own program grows its herbs, so its trees and shrubs take the order's, which gives the values its species leave unset, as the broadleaf program's defaults until then.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full, as Leguminosae: calyx synsepalous, 5-toothed or cleft; corolla of 5 petals, regular or somewhat irregular or commonly papilionaceous (so symmetry is each genus's); stamens 10, monadelphous, diadelphous or distinct (Acacia numerous); pistil 1, superior, 1-celled.

traits.leaf_division.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 27 Caesalpiniaceae and 28 Mimosaceae, which APG joins with his Papilionaceae as Fabaceae: leaves pinnate or bipinnate, rarely simple or of one leaflet; fruit a legume or one that does not split.

generator.params.leaf_length.why: A palmate leaf is its petiole and a leaflet end to end, so a herb's longest leaf is as long as its flora's petioles and leaflets together.

generator.params.basal_length.why: A palmate basal leaf is its petiole and a leaflet end to end, as a stem leaf is.

appearance.organs.*.shape.petiole.why: A palmate leaf's card is its petiole and a leaflet end to end, so the petiole's share is its length over theirs together.
